A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BackSplit and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–K. All 23 pages of each version support comparison, including material relocated during reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original lesion-segmentation experiments across five datasets, with quantitative comparisons, ablations, fine-tuning analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results using pretrained TotalSegmentator-CT initialization in Appendix J, Table 13.

M1.justification: BackSplit retains the same background subdivision, joint auxiliary-class supervision, losses, and inference approach. The pretrained-initialization experiment evaluates the existing method under another training setting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five evaluation datasets and AbdomenAtlas-derived auxiliary supervision. Table 13 reuses the KiTS23 and NSCLC-Radiomics tasks; its initialization change does not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing regular-training and virtual-class comparisons are retained. Table 13 applies another initialization to both regular training and BackSplit, preserving that comparator pair. MultiTalent is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix J adds TotalSegmentator-CT initialization followed by the previously described fine-tuning protocol on KiTS23 and NSCLC-Radiomics, alongside random-initialization results. Previously reported splits, metrics, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 13 adds a focused test of whether BackSplit's benefits persist with pretrained representations. Existing analyses of batch size, patch size, deep supervision, auxiliary-class count, partial supervision, and fine-tuning are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. Table 13 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–12 and Figures 1–8 are retained. New Table 13 reports regular/BackSplit Dice of 0.36/0.4072 on KiTS23 and 0.4716/0.5004 on NSCLC-Radiomics with TotalSegmentator-CT initialization. These are additional settings, not improved versions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same definitions, regularity assumptions, score-projection lemma, Fisher-information theorem, efficiency corollary, softmax proposition, and proofs. Extraction differences in mathematical encoding do not represent changed mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about structured background supervision, Fisher information, architectural generality, and effectiveness with imperfect auxiliary labels.

C2.justification: New Appendices B.1–B.2 explicitly discuss limited auxiliary-label availability in less common domains and unresolved effects of anatomical proximity, enclosure, and lesion size. Appendix J additionally interprets Table 13 as evidence that BackSplit complements pretrained representations.

D1.justification: Appendix C replaces the promise of a future code-and-weights release with a concrete repository link and an availability statement. The abstract adds a project-page link. These are documented access improvements; linked contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MultiTalent paper by Ulrich et al. as context for pretrained initialization in Appendix J. Existing related-work discussions and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds two short appendix subsections, expands Appendix J, updates the contents list, and makes limited wording edits. The main narrative and overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 13, shortens Table 4's caption, and relocates existing displays during appendix reflow, including Figures 4 and 6. Existing figures and table designs are retained, without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 13 supplies limited additional evidence for usefulness with pretrained initialization. Appendices B.1–B.2 clarify practical applicability and unresolved auxiliary-selection questions, while Appendix C supplies concrete access information previously deferred to publication. These improve practical usefulness and clarity, with the method, theory, and established experimental evidence otherwise unchanged.
